case_summary.summary: Reviewer accepted removal of the redundant equipment/location descriptor nodes and their connecting descriptive edge, but rejected removal of the phase condition node and its anchoring material-property edge, indicating that phase information was treated as useful explanatory context rather than dispensable redundancy.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Delete the standalone location node "bucket elevator #12".
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Delete standalone equipment or location descriptors when event nodes already carry the mechanism and the node has no needed supported causal role.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: If a location node only labels where events occur and adds no distinct causal structure, remove it.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Delete the standalone motor descriptor node "bucket elevator #12 motor".
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Delete descriptive component nodes that form an equipment island when the actual mechanism is already represented by event nodes.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Remove equipment-part nodes when failure or ignition events already represent their causal role.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Remove the descriptive "has" edge from "bucket elevator #12" to "bucket elevator #12 motor".
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Remove descriptive component edges when both endpoints are redundant descriptors rather than needed causal nodes.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: When both connected descriptor nodes are accepted for deletion, delete the purely descriptive edge between them too.

planning_patterns.reviewer_reason: The phase sould be identified as it is better for people to understand the phase of the released material
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Do not delete a material-condition descriptor when reviewers judge it necessary for understanding the released material, even if its direct causal role is limited.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Do not remove phase information when it is needed as explanatory context for interpreting the material involved.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Remove the "has" edge from "fine iron dust" to "Solid".
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Do not remove a defining descriptor edge when the connected descriptor node is retained.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: If a condition node stays, keep the edge that anchors that condition to the material unless there is a separate reason to remove it.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: Standalone location descriptor with no downstream causal use.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: This was treated as redundant descriptive context rather than a missing causal element because the operative pathway was already represented by event nodes.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Standalone equipment or location descriptors without needed supported causal roles should be diagnosed as redundancy.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Diagnose equipment-location labels outside the mechanism as surplus description when event nodes already localize the pathway.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: Component node isolated from the mechanism except by description.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: The reviewer outcome implies that the motor descriptor belonged to a descriptive equipment island, while the real mechanism was already captured by failure and ignition events.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Descriptive component nodes that do not add a distinct supported role should be diagnosed as redundant.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: If an equipment-part node only restates where an event occurs, diagnose it as descriptive redundancy.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: Descriptive edge connecting redundant equipment descriptors.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: The edge was treated as derivative redundancy rather than as an independent modeling problem because it only linked nodes that did not need to remain.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: When connected nodes are redundant descriptors, the descriptive edge between them is also redundant.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Diagnose descriptive edges as secondary redundancy when they only connect nodes that should not remain.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: Material phase descriptor retained for interpretive value.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: The reviewer treated phase as meaningful explanatory context, so the issue should not be framed as automatic redundancy just because the node originally appeared weakly integrated.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: A descriptor should only be diagnosed as redundant when it lacks a needed supported role; if it is needed to interpret the material involved, keep it in scope.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Be cautious diagnosing phase or property nodes as redundant when they help users understand the released material.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: Attribute edge retained because the descriptor remained in scope.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: Once the phase descriptor was considered valid to keep, its material-to-condition link was no longer best framed as standalone redundancy.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Remove a descriptor edge only when the descriptor it anchors is being removed as redundant.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Do not diagnose a material-to-property link as redundant if the property node itself is still considered necessary.

coverage_notes: Acceptance of the En2->En3 edge deletion was implicitly covered by acceptance of deleting both endpoint nodes.
Rejection of the En1->C1 edge deletion directly followed from rejection of deleting C1.
The updated graph added a new C1->Ev1 edge after review, which was not part of the planned suggestions and appears to have been used to better integrate the retained phase node.
